claims.text: The fare charges SGD 2.00 for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road at 08:33, but this trip's own trace never goes near it: the closest of the 104 fixes, at 08:34:30, is 1,843.93 m from the gantry's recorded coordinates, and no fix lies anywhere within the 250 m radius that POL-RD-09(4) treats as a crossing. A charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding.

The SGD 2.00 has no counterpart on any account of this trip. The platform's own booking route itemised ERP of SGD 0.00, and the fare breakdown's ERP block records the charged gantry as not on the optimal route - SGD 2.00 off-optimal against SGD 0.00 on-optimal, with off_optimal_route_total of 2.00. Nothing in the bundle places the vehicle on the CTE, and the driver's own account on file is that he used Upper Thomson and never the CTE. The line is a phantom pass-through and falls squarely within POL-RD-09(4).

That absence of a CTE crossing cannot be written off as a data gap. The trace carries 104 fixes at a 10 s cadence from 08:21:50 to 08:38:57, with a largest interval of 10 s, no straight-line step above 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 s, so it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); the vehicle's failure to approach the gantry is a real absence, not a hole in the record. The same trace is the governing distance measurement under POL-RD-01, and it is the trace figure that is used below.

On the trace figure that POL-RD-01 makes governing, the excess over the 8.7 km booked optimal is 1.14 km, or 13.1% of optimal - below the 20% establishment gate, so no route deviation is established, no POL-RD-02 recomputation of the distance and time lines runs, and the rider's '4-5 km extra' estimate is not made out. That finding does not empty the rider's case: POL-RD-01 expressly preserves a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) where neither establishment test is met, and it is on that limb - the SGD 2.00 CTE line charged for a gantry the trace never crosses - that the rider recovers on this trip.

The CTE line is refunded standalone and is not absorbed by any other limb: because no POL-RD-02 refund runs on this trip, POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule does not comprehend it, and POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out of its escalation trigger a charge line refunded under POL-RD-09(4). The case is therefore one that is decided with money moving on the disputed line, not one that escalates and leaves the amount held.

claims.text: The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy: POL-RD-01 provides that gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs, and it is 9.84 km (EV-GPS-04006); trip_record.actual_distance_km of 9.8 km may NOT be cited for the threshold test. Optimal distance at booking is 8.7 km (EV-TRIP-04006). Excess is therefore 1.14 km, which is 13.10% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; the percentage limb fails outright, so no route deviation exists on this trip and the outcome on the distance and time charges is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the morning.

The rider's account - a loop round Yio Chu Kang, 'must be 4-5km extra', a fare that should have been 12-13 - is unsupported by any artifact in the bundle and is contradicted by the only measurement on file: 9.84 km driven against an 8.7 km optimal route, an excess of 1.14 km, roughly a quarter of what is asserted. The planned route itself (Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Marymount Rd, Thomson Rd, Sinaran Dr) is the ordinary AMK-to-Novena corridor and matches the driver's statement that he took Upper Thomson and Thomson Road. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden of showing an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, and the same clause provides that an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 104 fixes at a 10.0 s cadence from 08:21:50 to 08:38:57, no gap between consecutive fixes larger than 10 s, largest straight-line step 114.0 m, highest implied speed 41.0 km/h - every one of these is far inside the 90 s gap, 500 m jump and 30 s sustained-sampling limbs. The 1.14 km excess is therefore sound as measured, no independent corroboration is required of it, and POL-RD-10(3) has nothing to bite on.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory at all, and the artifact minted for it, EV-ADVIS-04006-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; per POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact can carry no fact and its absence is itself citable. Neither party cites that identifier or asserts an external traffic cause - the driver's statement is that he took the normal way, not that a road was closed - so under POL-RD-13 there is no assertion to test against it, POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable, and nothing in a missing advisory can supply an amended optimal route or a justified excess. Because no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact, this is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it does not escalate the case under POL-RD-10(5).

On the one line the driver cannot defend, he does not try. The fare_breakdown carries a SGD 2.00 ERP line for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road, at 1.3412, 103.8559, charged at 08:33:00; the nearest fix on the trace is 1,843.93 m away (index 76, 08:34:30) and no gap brackets a closest approach, so the vehicle never came within the 250 m match radius that POL-RD-09(4) applies. That is a standalone billing-integrity correction, refundable whether or not a deviation exists, and the driver's own counterparty statement says as much ('Never go CTE. The ERP charge not from me.'). It is a government pass-through that was never the driver's money; it is refunded as it stands, and it leaves the SGD 12.14 of distance and time charges (7.38 + 4.76) on this metered fare untouched.

POL-RD-02 is a remedy that runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. No deviation is established here, so no recomputation is reached, the arithmetic of the optimal-route fare is never engaged, and no distance or time refund is available to the rider on the contested amount. In any event the metered lines are unimpeachable: 9.84 km at 0.75 per km and 17 min at 0.28 per min, with the surge multiplier of 1.0 read off fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, reconcile to the cent with the ledger and to the same trace that produced them.

The excess of 1.14 km at 13.10% is neither established nor material - materiality requires more than 50% of optimal or more than 8.0 km absolute - so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered at all; and consulted anyway it returns the same answer: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 295, a ratio of 0.000 against a pattern threshold of 0.05. There is therefore no basis for a FULL_REFUND uplift on the remedy and no basis for a driver-conduct referral. The remaining profile fields (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, prior_disputes_filed) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not ground any finding.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this case must be ruled and not held. Trip identifier TRP-04006 matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown; the timestamps are causally ordered and the trace's first and last fixes equal started_at and ended_at to the second (08:21:50, 08:38:57); the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); no exculpatory clause is invoked against any cited artifact; the identifiers on the three artifacts agree; any refund computable on these figures is a small fraction of the SGD 18.74 charged and nowhere near the SGD 150.00 ceiling or the charged total; and the only unmatched charge line in the fare_breakdown is the ERP line dealt with under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts.

The outcome the driver seeks is NO_ACTION on the rider's contested amount. The rider filed; payment_status on the fare_breakdown is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves the present payment state exactly as it stands - it never restores a charge and never converts an unsupported claim into a payout. The only movement the record supports is the SGD 2.00 pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(4), which costs the driver nothing and does not disturb the SGD 12.14 of distance and time fares this trip actually earned.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you should read this the same way: the distance and time charges for the ride stand, the SGD 2.00 CTE ERP line comes off, and SGD 2.00 is refunded to the rider.

What the trip shows. This is trip TRP-04006; the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry that identifier and agree on the timestamps. The platform's booked optimal route from Ang Mo Kio Ave 6 to Novena Medical Center was 8.7 km (EV-TRIP-04006). The governing distance is the GPS trace figure of 9.84 km (EV-GPS-04006), not the rounded 9.8 km convenience copy on the trip record, because POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern. Excess = 9.84 - 8.7 = 1.14 km, which is 13.1% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The 13.1% fails the percentage test, so no route deviation is established, however the morning felt and whatever a usual fare has been.

What follows for the contested amount. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation is never reached, and the distance charge (9.84 km x SGD 0.75 = SGD 7.38) and time charge (17 min x SGD 0.28 = SGD 4.76) stand as billed. The ledger reconciles to the cent: 3.80 base + 7.38 + 4.76 + 2.00 ERP + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 18.74 charged.

The one line that cannot stand. The SGD 2.00 ERP charge for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road, charged at 08:33, is for a gantry the trace never passes: the closest of the 104 fixes, at 08:34:30, is 1,843.93 m from the gantry's recorded coordinates, far outside the 250 m radius POL-RD-09(4) treats as a crossing. The booking route itemised ERP of SGD 0.00, and the fare block itself marks the line as off the optimal route (SGD 2.00 off-optimal against SGD 0.00 on-optimal). Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge for a gantry the trace never crosses is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists — and POL-RD-01 expressly preserves that limb where neither establishment test is met. Because no POL-RD-02 refund runs, nothing is double-counted (POL-RD-09(1)); and POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), so this case is ruled rather than held.

The accounts of both parties. The driver's statement that he went by Upper Thomson and Thomson Road and never used the CTE agrees with the planned corridor on the record (Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, Ave 1, Marymount Rd, Thomson Rd, Sinaran Dr) and with the trace, which never approaches the gantry; it is consistent with the ruling but is not what carries it. The rider's account of a loop round Yio Chu Kang and '4-5 km extra' is supported by no artifact in the bundle and is contradicted by the only measurement on file (1.14 km, not 4-5 km); under POL-RD-08 an assertion unsupported by evidence carries no weight. The driver's submission that the rider's claim be met with NO_ACTION is rejected so far as it would leave the ERP line in place: the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND on the rider's contested amount.

Points checked and not used as grounds. No traffic advisory exists in the bundle — EV-ADVIS-04006-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — but neither party asserts an external traffic cause or cites that identifier, so under POL-RD-13 there is nothing to test against it, POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable, and no POL-RD-10(5) escalation arises. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 104 fixes at a 10 s cadence, largest interval 10 s, largest straight-line step 114.0 m, highest implied speed 41.0 km/h. So the gap consequences of POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) do not engage, and the absence of any CTE crossing is a real absence rather than a hole in the record. POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered, the deviation being neither established nor material, and consulted anyway it returns nothing: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 295 completed trips in 90 days, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The remaining profile fields mentioned on both sides (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, prior_disputes_filed) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground nothing here. POL-RD-04's compensation limb is not available: the billed distance (9.84 km) is not less than the trace distance, so there is no unbilled distance to pay for, and driver_compensation_sgd is null.

Amount and confidence. Contested SGD 6.00; refunded SGD 2.00, being the CTE ERP correction alone. Confidence is 0.9: the artifacts the ruling rests on — EV-GPS-04006, EV-TRIP-04006 and EV-FARE-04006 — all carry weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is nowhere near. The monetary effect (SGD 2.00) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 it executes automatically on issue; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The line is refunded in full as a standalone correction and is recorded here for billing-integrity review.

ruling.explanation:
Rider filed over trip TRP-04006 (Ang Mo Kio Ave 6 to Novena Medical Center, 25 Aug 2026), contesting SGD 6.00 of an SGD 18.74 charge. Two questions decide it: was the route a deviation, and was the SGD 2.00 CTE ERP line properly charged?

Route deviation — not established. POL-RD-01 measures excess as trace distance less the booked optimal. The governing trace figure (EV-GPS-04006) is 9.84 km; the trip record (EV-TRIP-04006) books the optimal route at 8.7 km with 15 min and ERP 0.00. Excess is 1.14 km, which is 13.1% of optimal. A deviation is established only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The 0.8 km limb passes (1.14 km) but the percentage limb fails (13.1% < 20%), so no deviation exists and the distance and time charges stand. Your estimate of 4-5 km extra is not supported: the recorded excess is roughly a quarter of that, and the trace is clean — 104 fixes at a 10 s cadence from 08:21:50 to 08:38:57, no interval above 10 s, largest straight-line step 114 m, so there is no gap in which a loop round Yio Chu Kang could have hidden. The 'went round by Yio Chu Kang' account cites no artifact and is outweighed by the trace. The driver's account of the route (Upper Thomson, then Thomson Road) matches the corridor planned at booking. No POL-RD-02 recomputation runs, and the SGD 14.525 of distance-and-time charges remain payable.

ERP line — refunded. EV-FARE-04006 carries SGD 2.00 for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road, charged 08:33. The gantry's coordinates are 1.3412, 103.8559; the closest fix on the trace is 1,843.93 m away, far outside the 250 m radius POL-RD-09(4) treats as a crossing, and no gap brackets a closer approach. A charge for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, whether or not a deviation exists. It is a government pass-through rather than driver revenue, so refunding it does not touch the SGD 12.14 of fares this trip earned. Because no POL-RD-02 refund runs, POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule does not absorb it, and POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4) from escalation.

Outcome. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.00 to the rider — SGD 2.00 of the SGD 6.00 claimed, and SGD 16.74 of the SGD 18.74 charged remaining payable. The driver is right that no deviation is established and the distance and time charges stand, but because part of the contested amount moves back to the rider, POL-GEN-03 makes the outcome PARTIAL_REFUND rather than NO_ACTION. No driver compensation is due: the distance billed (9.84 km) equals the trace distance, so POL-RD-04's unbilled-distance limb does not arise (and no rider-requested detour appears in the chat log, whose only messages are 'Here already, at the void deck' and 'coming', with no waypoint hint). POL-RD-06 is not triggered — the excess is neither established nor material — and consulted anyway, EV-DPROF-04006 shows deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 295, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The remaining profile fields (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, prior_disputes_filed) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground no finding here.

Confidence and escalation. Confidence 0.95: every artifact carrying a deciding fact — EV-GPS-04006 and EV-FARE-04006, and EV-TRIP-04006 for the booked optimal — carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-04006-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); nothing in this ruling rests on it, no party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged (POL-RD-13). The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), the identifiers on all three artifacts agree, the timestamps are causally ordered, the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total, and the only unmatched charge line is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) excepts — so no POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case is ruled, not held. The monetary effect (SGD 2.00) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue, subject to one appeal within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 ERP line in EV-FARE-04006 for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road (charged 08:33, at 1.3412, 103.8559) is a charge for a gantry the trip's GPS trace never crossed — the nearest of the 104 fixes on EV-GPS-04006 is 1,843.93 m away, far outside the 250 m match radius, and no gap brackets a closer approach. The line is refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction and is recorded here as a billing-integrity finding.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this dispute has two parts, and they come out differently.

1. The route (rider's '4-5 km extra'). POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace, not the rounded copy, the governing measurement. The trace (EV-GPS-04006) measures 9.84 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the platform's booking route (EV-TRIP-04006) was 8.7 km. The excess is 1.14 km, which is 13.1% of the optimal distance. A deviation is established only where the excess is BOTH more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal; 1.14 km clears the absolute test but 13.1% does not clear the 20% gate. No deviation is established, so no POL-RD-02 recomputation of the distance and time lines runs, and the rider's estimate of 4-5 km extra is not supported by any artifact in the bundle (POL-RD-08: the excess shown is less than a quarter of what was asserted). The driver's account that he used Upper Thomson / Thomson Road is consistent with the planned route on the trip record. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 104 fixes at 10.0 s spacing, largest interval 10 s, largest step 114.0 m, highest implied speed 41.0 km/h. The distance charge of SGD 7.38 (9.84 km x 0.75) and time charge of SGD 4.76 (17 min x 0.28) therefore stand.

2. The SGD 2.00 CTE ERP line (the rider's stronger point, and the driver concedes it). The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-04006) charges SGD 2.00 for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road at 08:33, with the gantry's coordinates on the record. The closest of the trace's 104 fixes, at 08:34:30, is 1,843.93 m from those coordinates — far outside the 250 m radius POL-RD-09(4) treats as a crossing. The vehicle never crossed that gantry, so the line is a phantom pass-through. POL-RD-09(4) makes it refundable in full as a standalone correction, whether or not a deviation exists, and because no deviation refund runs here, POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule does not absorb it. The driver's own statement on file agrees the ERP charge was not his.

Money. Charged total: SGD 18.74. Refund to the rider: SGD 2.00 (the ERP line, already a multiple of SGD 0.05). Remaining charge: SGD 16.74, comprising base fare SGD 3.80, distance SGD 7.38, time SGD 4.76 and platform fee SGD 0.80. The SGD 2.00 is one third of the SGD 6.00 claimed, so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not a full one; on the distance and time lines the driver's NO_ACTION position is upheld and the present payment state stands.

Other points. EV-ADVIS-04006-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and can carry no fact; no party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-13/POL-RD-03 have nothing to test and the missing advisory neither helps nor escalates. The profile check under POL-RD-06 is not triggered (the excess is neither established nor material), and it would return no pattern in any event (deviation_flags_90d 0 of 295 completed trips in 90 days). No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers match, timestamps are causally ordered and agree to the second, the trace is unimpaired, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact, and the only unmatched charge line is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. Confidence is 0.92, the deciding facts resting on artifacts at weight 1.0. The monetary effect (SGD 2.00) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it is executed automatically; both parties keep the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
Rider: you were right about one line and it has been refunded — SGD 2.00. Driver: the rest of the fare stands, and neither of you is at fault for the rest.

DISTANCE AND TIME — NO REFUND. Trip TRP-04006 ran from Ang Mo Kio Ave 6 to Novena Medical Center. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the GPS trace EV-GPS-04006, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record: the trace measures 9.84 km against a booked optimal of 8.7 km (EV-TRIP-04006). The excess is 1.14 km, which is 13.10% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH more than 20% of the optimal distance AND more than 0.8 km. The absolute limb passes, but the percentage limb fails by a wide margin, so no route deviation is established on this trip, however the morning felt and however the trip was characterised. Your estimate of '4-5 km extra' is not supported by anything in the bundle — the only measurement on file shows roughly a quarter of that — and the route the platform recorded at booking (Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, Ave 1, Marymount Rd, Thomson Rd, Sinaran Dr) is the ordinary AMK-to-Novena corridor, consistent with the driver's account that he used Upper Thomson and Thomson Road. No evidence supports a loop round Yio Chu Kang.

Because no deviation is established, the POL-RD-02 recomputation never runs and no recomputed fare is produced; there is therefore no distance or time refund. The metered lines stand exactly as billed: base fare SGD 3.80, distance 9.84 km at SGD 0.75 = SGD 7.38, time 17 min at SGD 0.28 = SGD 4.76, platform fee SGD 0.80; charged_total SGD 18.74 (EV-FARE-04006), payment status CHARGED, nothing refunded so far. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 104 fixes at a 10-second cadence from 08:21:50 to 08:38:57, largest interval 10 s, largest step 114 m, no sustained sampling above 30 s — so the 1.14 km figure is sound, no independent corroboration is required, and nothing escalates on trace integrity.

THE ERP LINE — REFUNDED. The one line that does not survive is the SGD 2.00 charge for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road (EV-FARE-04006, charged 08:33:00 at 1.3412, 103.8559). POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing. The closest approach on the whole trace is 1,843.93 m (fix 76, 08:34:30), and no pair of fixes brackets a closer approach. The vehicle never crossed that gantry. The platform's own booking route itemised ERP of SGD 0.00, the fare breakdown itself records the gantry as off-optimal (SGD 2.00 off-optimal against SGD 0.00 on-optimal), and the driver's own statement accepts the charge was not his ('Never go CTE. The ERP charge not from me.'). That is a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and it is not added on top of anything — no POL-RD-02 refund runs, so there is no double counting.

OTHER POINTS. No traffic advisory was on file: EV-ADVIS-04006-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable. Neither party asserted an external traffic cause (a closure, a queue, a breakdown), so nothing was invoked against the missing artifact and its absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction — under POL-RD-13 it neither reduces the excess nor escalates the case, and no POL-RD-10(5) trigger fires. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires either: the trip identifier matches across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, the timestamps are causally ordered and the trace's first and last fixes equal started_at and ended_at to the second, the refund is far under the SGD 150.00 ceiling, and the only unmatched charge line is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. This case is decided, not held.

DRIVER CONDUCT AND COMPENSATION. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: the deviation is neither established nor material (materiality needs over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km). Consulted anyway, it returns the same answer — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 295 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern exists, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies and no driver-conduct referral is made. The other profile fields mentioned in the arguments — rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, prior_disputes_filed, acceptance_rate, account_age_days — are context only under POL-GEN-01, no finding rests on them, and they were not used. No driver compensation is due: the rider was billed for the full 9.84 km the trace records, so POL-RD-04's unbilled-distance limb has no shortfall to work on.

FIGURES USED. Charged total SGD 18.74 (EV-FARE-04006); refund to the rider SGD 2.00 (the ERP line); driver compensation nil; the SGD 12.14 of distance and time charges earned on this trip stand. The monetary effect is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the SGD 2.00 is released on issue. This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The fare charges SGD 2.00 for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road at 08:33, but this trip's own trace never goes near it: the closest of the 104 fixes, at 08:34:30, is 1,843.93 m from the gantry's recorded coordinates, and no fix lies anywhere within the 250 m radius that POL-RD-09(4) treats as a crossing. A charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding.

The SGD 2.00 has no counterpart on any account of this trip. The platform's own booking route itemised ERP of SGD 0.00, and the fare breakdown's ERP block records the charged gantry as not on the optimal route - SGD 2.00 off-optimal against SGD 0.00 on-optimal, with off_optimal_route_total of 2.00. Nothing in the bundle places the vehicle on the CTE, and the driver's own account on file is that he used Upper Thomson and never the CTE. The line is a phantom pass-through and falls squarely within POL-RD-09(4).

That absence of a CTE crossing cannot be written off as a data gap. The trace carries 104 fixes at a 10 s cadence from 08:21:50 to 08:38:57, with a largest interval of 10 s, no straight-line step above 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 s, so it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); the vehicle's failure to approach the gantry is a real absence, not a hole in the record. The same trace is the governing distance measurement under POL-RD-01, and it is the trace figure that is used below.

On the trace figure that POL-RD-01 makes governing, the excess over the 8.7 km booked optimal is 1.14 km, or 13.1% of optimal - below the 20% establishment gate, so no route deviation is established, no POL-RD-02 recomputation of the distance and time lines runs, and the rider's '4-5 km extra' estimate is not made out. That finding does not empty the rider's case: POL-RD-01 expressly preserves a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) where neither establishment test is met, and it is on that limb - the SGD 2.00 CTE line charged for a gantry the trace never crosses - that the rider recovers on this trip.

The CTE line is refunded standalone and is not absorbed by any other limb: because no POL-RD-02 refund runs on this trip, POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule does not comprehend it, and POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out of its escalation trigger a charge line refunded under POL-RD-09(4). The case is therefore one that is decided with money moving on the disputed line, not one that escalates and leaves the amount held.

The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy: POL-RD-01 provides that gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs, and it is 9.84 km (EV-GPS-04006); trip_record.actual_distance_km of 9.8 km may NOT be cited for the threshold test. Optimal distance at booking is 8.7 km (EV-TRIP-04006). Excess is therefore 1.14 km, which is 13.10% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; the percentage limb fails outright, so no route deviation exists on this trip and the outcome on the distance and time charges is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the morning.

The rider's account - a loop round Yio Chu Kang, 'must be 4-5km extra', a fare that should have been 12-13 - is unsupported by any artifact in the bundle and is contradicted by the only measurement on file: 9.84 km driven against an 8.7 km optimal route, an excess of 1.14 km, roughly a quarter of what is asserted. The planned route itself (Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Marymount Rd, Thomson Rd, Sinaran Dr) is the ordinary AMK-to-Novena corridor and matches the driver's statement that he took Upper Thomson and Thomson Road. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden of showing an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, and the same clause provides that an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 104 fixes at a 10.0 s cadence from 08:21:50 to 08:38:57, no gap between consecutive fixes larger than 10 s, largest straight-line step 114.0 m, highest implied speed 41.0 km/h - every one of these is far inside the 90 s gap, 500 m jump and 30 s sustained-sampling limbs. The 1.14 km excess is therefore sound as measured, no independent corroboration is required of it, and POL-RD-10(3) has nothing to bite on.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory at all, and the artifact minted for it, EV-ADVIS-04006-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; per POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact can carry no fact and its absence is itself citable. Neither party cites that identifier or asserts an external traffic cause - the driver's statement is that he took the normal way, not that a road was closed - so under POL-RD-13 there is no assertion to test against it, POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable, and nothing in a missing advisory can supply an amended optimal route or a justified excess. It is a government pass-through that was never the driver's money; it is refunded as it stands, and it leaves the SGD 12.14 of distance and time charges (7.38 + 4.76) on this metered fare untouched.

POL-RD-02 is a remedy that runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. No deviation is established here, so no recomputation is reached, the arithmetic of the optimal-route fare is never engaged, and no distance or time refund is available to the rider on the contested amount.
